source.title_on_document: We're Different, We're the Same: Creative Homogeneity Across LLMs

supplement.where: No separate supplement is cited. Appendices A (test wording), B (originality scoring formulas), and C (t-SNE of FF and DAT) are in this PDF, pp. 16-18.
supplement.holds: Appendices hold prompt wording, scoring formulas, and Figure 10 only; no extra statistics.

paper_design_summary: The authors give three divergent-thinking tests (Alternative Uses Task, Forward Flow, Divergent Association Task) to 22 large language models and to 102 Prolific participants who worked without AI. They compare individual originality scores (GloVe semantic distance) and population-level variability (cosine distance between sentence embeddings of different respondents' answers) between the LLM set (main analysis: 7 models, one per family) and the human set. No person receives AI assistance; additional analyses vary LLM prompt wording and system prompts, compare a Llama-only model set with the cross-family set, and compare the Prolific humans with public datasets of humans from prior studies.

studies.label: LLM responses vs Prolific human responses on AUT, FF, and DAT

assignment.what_was_assigned: Nothing was assigned to people. Humans completed the tests without AI; LLMs were prompted separately with the same tests.
assignment.quote: To study this question, we elicit creative responses from humans and a broad set of LLMs using standardized creativity tests and compare the population-level diversity of responses.
assignment.locator: p. 1, Abstract; p. 4-5, Section 3.3 Test subjects

arms.name: LLMs
arms.description: 22 LLMs queried through public APIs with the default system prompt 'You are a helpful assistant'; statistical tests on population-level variability use 7 models, one per family (AI21 Jamba 1.5 Large, Google Gemini 1.5, Cohere Command R Plus, Meta Llama 3 70B Instruct, Mistral Large, gpt 4o, Phi 3 medium 128k Instruct). AI-generated output, not people.

arms.name: Humans (Prolific)
arms.description: Prolific participants who completed the DAT, FF, and AUT in a survey, with no AI assistance.

participants.exclusions: 114 recruited; 12 removed on suspicion of being bots (response time under 5 minutes) or failed attention checks; 102 retained. No randomization; 114 is the number recruited.
participants.who: Prolific workers screened for English fluency and approval rating above 95; paid $15/hour; average completion time 19 minutes. Demographics in Table 1 (51% female, 53% White).
participants.quote: We recruited 114 initial participants from the Prolific platform, screening for English fluency and an approval rating > 95. Of these, 12 were removed on suspicion of being bots

ai_tool.name_model: 22 LLMs including AI21 Jamba Instruct, Cohere Command R / R Plus, Meta Llama 3/3.1 family, Mistral large/Nemo/small, Google Gemini 1.5, gpt 4o, gpt 4o mini, Phi 3/3.5 family (list on pp. 4-5); main tests use 7 models, one per family
ai_tool.how_used: LLMs answer the creativity tests themselves; their outputs are compared with human outputs. No person uses AI.

task.description: Alternative Uses Task with five objects (book, fork, table, hammer, pants; up to 10 uses each), Forward Flow with five start words (candle, table, bear, snow, toaster; up to 20 words), and the Divergent Association Task (10 unrelated nouns, under four minutes).
task.duration: Humans took 19 minutes on average to complete the survey.

outcomes.name: Population-level response variability V_t (cosine distance between sentence embeddings of different respondents' responses to the same prompt)
outcomes.question: none
outcomes.measure_detail: 1 minus cosine similarity of all-MiniLM-L6-v2 sentence embeddings between the full responses of two different population members to the same prompt; punctuation and stopwords removed. Robustness variants: AUT prompt versions v1-v3 and v3 single-word answers only (Table 5, p. 11); system prompts baseline, more creative, very creative, not creative (Table 7, p. 13); Llama family vs cross-family set (Table 6, recorded in S3).

contrasts.treatment_arm: LLMs (7 models, one per family, default system prompt, AUT prompt v3)
contrasts.reported: Table 3: AUT mu(V(LLM)) 0.459 vs mu(V(Human)) 0.738, t(10078) = 19.1, p = 3.9e-80, effect size 2.2, power 1.0; FF 0.534 vs 0.835, t(90) = 26.1, p = 2.8e-66, effect size 2.0, power 1.0; DAT 0.665 vs 0.819, t(30) = 9.9, p = 6.2e-11, effect size 1.4, power 1.0. Higher value = more variability; LLMs less diverse.

contrasts.treatment_arm: LLMs under AUT prompt versions v1, v2, v3, v3 single-word answers
LLMs under system prompts Baseline / More creative / Very creative / Not creative (AUT)
contrasts.reported: Table 7 population-level variability: Humans 0.738; Baseline 0.459, t(10078) = 19.1, 3.9e-80; More creative 0.503, t(10078) = 16.1, 3.5e-58; Very creative 0.576, t(10078) = 11.1, 5.6e-29; Not creative 0.492, t(10078) = 16.8, 1.1e-62.

diversity_detail.metric: Cosine distance (1 - cosine similarity) between sentence embeddings of two respondents' full responses to the same prompt; population mean mu(V_t)
diversity_detail.computed_over: All pairs of different population members (LLM-LLM pairs within the LLM set, human-human pairs within the human set) for each prompt
diversity_detail.uncertainty: Welch's t-test on pair-level distance scores (pairs treated as independent); significance threshold 0.01; Cohen's d with pooled SD and test power reported
diversity_detail.notes: Equation 1, p. 6. The AUT response is all of a respondent's uses for one object joined into one string.

outcomes.name: Individual originality score O_t (semantic distance via GloVe word embeddings)
outcomes.question: none
outcomes.measure_detail: GloVe 840B word embeddings. AUT: TF-IDF weighted mean of 1 - cosine(prompt, word); FF: mean forward flow distance; DAT: mean pairwise distance among the 10 words (Appendix B, p. 18). Robustness variants: AUT prompt versions v1-v3 (Table 4, p. 10) and system prompts (Table 7, p. 13).

contrasts.treatment_arm: LLMs (default system prompt, AUT prompt v3)
contrasts.reported: Table 2: AUT mu(O(LLM)) 0.711 vs mu(O(Human)) 0.696, t(2094) = -3.4, p = 0.001, effect size 0.1, power 0.84; FF 0.603 vs 0.637, t(164) = 5.2, p = 2.9e-07, effect size 0.52, power 0.99; DAT 0.801 vs 0.753, t(159) = -5.12, p = 8.7e-07, effect size 0.77, power 0.99. LLMs higher on AUT and DAT, lower on FF.

contrasts.treatment_arm: LLMs under AUT prompt versions v1, v2, v3
LLMs under system prompts Baseline / More creative / Very creative / Not creative (AUT)
contrasts.reported: Table 7 individual creativity: Humans 0.695; Baseline 0.711, t(2094) = -3.4, 0.001; More creative 0.733, t(5020) = -9.8, 1.0e-22; Very creative 0.754, t(5206) = -15.9, 3.2e-56; Not creative 0.702, t(2507) = -1.28, 0.1.

outcomes.name: Word overlap between pairs of full responses
outcomes.question: none
outcomes.measure_detail: After removing stopwords, count of overlapping words between sets of responses from two LLMs or two humans (all AUT uses, all FF words, the DAT list); shown as the percent of response pairs with each number of overlapping words.

contrasts.reported: Figure 4: 'LLM responses have far more words in common than do human responses.' Histograms only; no test statistics. Direction coded on diversity (more overlap = less diverse).
contrasts.locator: p. 9, Figure 4; p. 8, 'One explanation: word overlap in LLM responses'

diversity_detail.metric: Number of overlapping non-stopwords between two respondents' full responses
diversity_detail.computed_over: Pairs of responses from different LLMs or from different humans
diversity_detail.notes: Descriptive explanation of the embedding result.

sample_overlap.shares_participants_with: S2 reuses public human datasets from prior creativity studies (osf.io/u3yv4, osf.io/7p5mt, osf.io/kbeq6) as a validation sample; these are not AI-assistance papers. The main Prolific sample is the authors' own.

company_involvement.description: None stated. Authors at Duke University and Technion.

eligibility.reason: No person receives AI assistance. The paper compares outputs generated by LLMs with outputs of 102 unassisted Prolific participants on divergent-thinking tests, so it is AI-versus-human context evidence (homogeneity of LLM outputs across models). Criterion 2 is met only in the sense that 102 humans were analyzed; no one was assigned to AI.

one_line_finding: Across AUT, FF, and DAT, responses from 7 LLMs (one per family) are far less variable than responses from 102 Prolific participants (mean cosine distance AUT 0.459 vs 0.738, FF 0.534 vs 0.835, DAT 0.665 vs 0.819; effect sizes 2.2, 2.0, 1.4; p. 8, Table 3), while individual originality is similar (Table 2, p. 7).
open_questions: Effect sizes and t-tests treat pairs of responses (or individual responses) as independent observations; the number of LLM outputs per model is not stated.
notes: LLM 'arm' counts models, not people: 22 models tested, 7 used for statistical tests. Arms[].ai coded generative_ai for the LLM output arm because it is AI-generated output; no person used AI. The sign of t-statistics in Tables 2, 4, 7 follows the paper (negative when LLMs score higher). Human ages, gender, race in Table 1, p. 5.
